### Rethinking Local News: How Sarah Alvarez Is Building Journalism in Support of Community Needs
Source: Nieman Reports
Published: 2026-11-11 13:00 UTC
URL: https://niemanreports.org/local-news-detroit-michigan-public-media-sarah-alvarez-founder-ceo-community-needs-foreclosures-outlier-media-documenters-city-bureau-chicago/
Source meta: reference_tool · aggregator · R3 · P4 · reference
Fetched: 2026-11-11 21:41 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Nieman Reports [media_lens] https://niemanreports.org/local-news-detroit-michigan-public-media-sarah-alvarez-founder-ceo-community-needs-foreclosures-outlier-media-documenters-city-bureau-chicago/

Sarah Alvarez has spent much of her career rethinking how local journalism can serve the public. After working as a civil rights attorney, then as a reporter and producer at the NPR station Michigan Public, she founded Outlier Media in 2016. Alvarez said the Detroit-based nonprofit newsroom was designed to fill information and accountability gaps in communities that were often overlooked by traditional news organizations.. One of its signature innovations, TXT OUTLIER, is a text message service Alvarez created to connect Detroiters directly with journalists and provide practical information on issues affecting their lives, from utility bills to housing and foreclosures. Under Alvarez’s leadership, Outlier also expanded its Documenters program, an initiative that trains and pays residents to attend and report on public meetings to create a public record of local government decisions in places that don’t have press coverage. The initiative has engaged more than 700 Detroiters and since spread nationwide, creating new opportunities for civic participation and public accountability.

With the first U.S. midterm elections since President Donald Trump’s return to the White House approaching, voters will be weighing in on a range of issues, from the economy and rising cost of living, to the administration’s foreign policy and the future direction of both major parties. At a recent virtual Nieman-to-Nieman seminar, a group of Nieman alums who cover politics discussed what they’re hearing from voters with regards to key Senate races, the growing influence of younger voters drawn to progressive candidates, and the political implications of conflicts involving Iran, Ukraine, and Russia. Moderated by Austin Bogues (NF ’21), news desk editor at USA Today, the discussion brought together James Barragán (NF ’24), political anchor for Spectrum News in Austin, Texas; Bill Barrow (NF ’22), national politics reporter for The Associated Press in Atlanta; and Ines Pohl (NF ’05), Washington bureau chief and White House correspondent for Deutsche Welle, Germany’s international public broadcaster.

As protests continue across India over allegations of government corruption, dozens of members of the media have been subjected to arrest, detainment and assault, according to witnesses, press rights organizations, and the journalists themselves. Thousands of protesters have taken to the streets of New Delhi in recent weeks, demanding the resignation of election officials allegedly tied to the deletion of nearly 130 million names from voter registration rolls. The protests — which have largely been organized by the Cockroach Janata Party, so named after India's chief justice called the nation’s unemployed youth and activists "cockroaches" — are part of a wider wave of youth discontent aimed at Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his administration. Organizers have mobilized young people via social media, tapping into frustrations with government corruption, eroding trust in democratic institutions, and a lack of access to jobs and educational opportunities.

The Trump administration’s latest attacks on the news media have followed a familiar pattern: President Donald Trump lashes out at news outlets for perceived bias and follows up with restrictive actions that appear blatantly unconstitutional; a judge’s ruling follows, temporarily halting the actions; and the administration pivots and pushes ahead with other restrictions. This time it was the removal of three outlets — CNN, MS NOW, and Politico — from White House press access in September. After the groups sued, and U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly issued a temporary restraining order restoring their access on Sept. 24, the administration barred CNN and Politico from providing pool coverage on trips outside Washington. Kelly issued a longer, preliminary injunction on Oct. 14, halting the administration from blocking the news organizations’ access to the White House while the case proceeds. My happiest times in journalism have been when I have built something new. For my latest venture, I want to help bring investigative journalism on climate and environmental issues to a much larger audience than it has reached in the past. To do so, I’m starting a brand-new newsroom focused on the environmental and climate crisis, and I’m taking my audience along for the ride. I’ll be documenting every facet of the process with an “open kitchen” approach of radical transparency, starting with a 100-day video countdown chronicling all the steps involved with starting a news organization from the ground up. This effort combines two of the things I’m most passionate about: I love digging up stories that other people don’t want to see published, and I love creating opportunities for other journalists. I’ve been a journalist for most of my life. I started working at age 14 for the local paper in my rural German town, turned to doing investigative stories in my early 20s, and later studied investigative journalism at the Columbia University Graduate School of Journalism in New York.

### America’s Shrinking Local Newsrooms, Through a Photographer’s Lens
Source: Nieman Reports
Published: 2026-10-02 12:30 UTC
URL: https://niemanreports.org/americas-shrinking-local-newsrooms-photographer-ann-hermes-local-news-news-deserts-rural-america/
Source meta: reference_tool · aggregator · R3 · P4 · reference

Attribution: Nieman Reports [media_lens] https://niemanreports.org/americas-shrinking-local-newsrooms-photographer-ann-hermes-local-news-news-deserts-rural-america/

For many journalists, the sight of empty desks is a sadly familiar one. My first glimpse of a gutted newsroom facing further cutbacks sparked a documentary photography project that has so far taken me to more than 50 newsrooms across the United States over the past eight years. It began when my mother, a loyal subscriber to our local metro in southern Illinois, told me a decade ago how disappointed she was in the newspaper. She complained that the local coverage was lacking, and the paper seemed to be thinner. Already several years into my photojournalism career, I was unsurprised by her remarks — I had been witnessing the decline of print media since graduation from journalism school. Still, my curiosity was piqued, and I arranged a visit to the paper to see for myself. Cue the scene of a barren newsroom. Not only were there empty desks, but also an expanse of exposed carpet with indentations showing where desks had once long stood. While there has been a great deal of reporting on the issues plaguing local journalism, I hadn’t seen the story told visually.

### 澳枪击事件嫌疑人为父子：曾宣誓效忠“伊斯兰国”，行凶枪支为合法持有
Source: The Paper 澎湃新闻
Published: 2025-12-16 02:23 UTC
URL: https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32178049
Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-11 21:41 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: The Paper 澎湃新闻 [global_news] https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32178049

据新华社12月15日援引澳大利亚广播公司报道，澳大利亚联合反恐小组调查人员表示，悉尼邦迪滩枪击事件两名嫌疑人曾宣誓效忠“伊斯兰国”恐怖组织。 报道援引联合反恐小组一名不愿透露姓名的高级官员的话说，警方在邦迪滩两名枪手车内发现一面“伊斯兰国”旗帜。澳大利亚安全情报组织6年前就已在调查邦迪滩枪击案两名枪手之一的纳维德·阿克拉姆，他与“伊斯兰国”在悉尼的恐怖分子有密切联系。 澳大利亚警方表示，枪击事件的两名嫌疑人是父子关系，使用合法获得的枪支发动了此次袭击事件。 澳大利亚总理阿尔巴尼斯15日表示：“今天下午4点， 我将把更严格的枪支法律列入国家内阁的议程，包括限制个人可持有或许可的枪支数量 。此外，还需对许可证进行定期审查。人们的情况会发生变化，人们的思想也会随着时间的推移而变得激进。许可证不应永久有效。” 此次枪击事件已造成包括1名作案嫌疑人在内的16人死亡、40人受伤。这是自1996年塔斯马尼亚州亚瑟港枪击事件造成35人死亡以来，澳大利亚发生的最严重的大规模枪击事件。 持有枪支许可证长达十年 据多家外媒报道，其中一名袭击者为24岁的澳大利亚公民纳维德·阿克拉姆，他在现场被捕，随后被送往悉尼的一家医院。另一名袭击者是他的父亲萨吉德·阿克拉姆，他于1998年来到澳大利亚，被警方当场击毙。 澳大利亚警方随后证实，纳维德·阿克拉姆此前已被新南威尔士州警方和其他机构记录在案。其父亲萨吉德·阿克拉姆持有枪支许可证，名下登记有6支枪，目前均已被追回。新南威尔士州警察局长马尔·兰永透露，萨吉德·阿克拉姆已持有枪支许可证长达十年。 阿尔巴尼斯在新闻发布会上透露，纳维德·阿克拉姆曾于2019年10月首次引起当局的注意。他补充说，对该男子进行检查是基于他与其他人有联系，但评估结果表明，没有任何迹象表明他存在持续的威胁或暴力倾向。 新南威尔士州州长克里斯·明斯表示，警方正在调查他们的系统是否存在故障，导致合法持有的武器可能被用于恐怖袭击。 枪手“性格古怪”，爱好打猎 据《卫报》澳大利亚版报道，纳维德·阿克拉姆在袭击前从事砌砖工作。他的同事表示，纳维德性格古怪，“没人和他亲近”。“（砌砖工人）在一起的时间很长，因为砌砖是一项非常枯燥乏味的工作，所以大家会聊很多话。但纳维德是一个性格很古怪的人……他工作非常努力，几乎没有休息日。” 尽管澳大利亚警方并未确认纳维德·阿克拉姆是否合法持有枪支，但据这位同事表示，纳维德经常外出打猎，曾提及在昆士兰州南部高原的克鲁克韦尔附近射杀兔子和其他猎物。这位同事还表示，就在几周前，纳维德告诉老板，他的手骨折了，所以要到2026年才能工作。

### 儿童手表“小天才圈”调查：点赞成每日功课，有商家可解除家长管控
Source: The Paper 澎湃新闻
Published: 2025-12-15 14:23 UTC
URL: https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32177210
Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-11 21:41 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: The Paper 澎湃新闻 [global_news] https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32177210

在校园里，孩子们时常举起戴在手腕上的手表，彼此一碰，便加为好友。 这种以“安全”为核心卖点的儿童电话手表，如今已超越通信工具的属性，悄然演变成一个拥有独特规则、社交层级甚至灰色产业链的未成年人数字社交圈——“小天才圈”。 在这个属于他们的“江湖”里，“大佬榜”备受关注，“扩列”（增加好友）成为新的社交需求，“点主”（在主页点赞）是每日必做的功课……这些让成年人感到陌生的词汇，正构筑着未成年人的数字社交世界。 然而，伴随着这种社交形态的兴起，家长们的担忧也日益加剧：孩子过度沉迷手表社交、不良信息传播、因品牌壁垒导致的“社交绑架”等问题逐渐浮现。《法治日报》记者近日对该现象展开调查，试图揭开这一未成年人数字社交圈的真实面貌。 点赞成社交“硬通货” 据北京“小天才圈”资深玩家陈曦（化名）介绍，圈内有5000余名活跃用户，多为11岁至17岁的学生，这个社交圈形成了一套精心设计的“混圈规则”。“入圈”需设定两个字的独特圈名，随后可在平台分享生活点滴，吸引具有相同爱好的好友进行互动；若想提升知名度或影响力，需每日经营主页并与好友动态互动。 记者注意到，在一些社交平台上，大量以“小天才圈交友攻略”为主题的内容应运而生，内容涵盖如何快速“扩列”、获取更多点赞等“实用”技巧，评论区有不少“留下ID互加好友”的留言。在这一社交体系中，点赞是这套规则的核心——平台设定每日主页获赞上限为3000个，若要达到“100万+”的“大佬”级别，需连续点赞近一年时间。围绕点赞数与知名度，圈内形成了清晰的“大佬排行榜”，点赞数也成为社交“硬通货”。 这种对点赞的追逐，已催生出相关服务产业。记者调查发现，某社交平台上，拥有数十万甚至上百万点赞数的账号，售价从几百元到上千元不等：100多万点赞的账号标价1300元，90多万点赞的账号标价1200元。 今年18岁的“灵师”（圈名），在2021年14岁时加入“小天才圈”，她的账号目前已拥有150个好友、超100万点赞量。她告诉记者，这样的账号市场价值约1000元。 “围绕点赞需求，还衍生出代刷赞、租账号、出售‘大佬好友位’等服务。”“灵师”进一步介绍，例如付费100元至180元，即可获得“bot”（记者注：“bot”是一种第三方开发的自动化工具，主要用于刷赞、修改记录和发送动态等功能，这类工具能帮助用户快速提升账号点赞数，从而在未成年人社交圈中获得更高地位）自动点赞功能——用户将手表寄给相关人员进行10天左右的处理便能完成安装。此后，发帖5分钟内即可自动获赞，还可以一键查询未点赞名单。

近日，总台接到群众举报，反映陈皮市场存在年份虚标、产地及工艺造假等问题，千元一斤的“年份陈皮”亦可能名不副实。 茶枝柑新果皮冒充陈皮 广西浦北出现“速成工艺陈皮” 记者发现，直播间里售卖陈皮低价轮番轰炸，年份承诺掷地有声。 直播间也有主播爆料，八成市面上所谓广东新会陈皮实为广西陈皮。 广西钦州市浦北县是茶枝柑重要种植基地，其果皮是陈皮风味“越陈越香”关键，也是浦北陈皮唯一原料。2024年当地陈皮产业产值破60亿元，采收季大量鲜果加工晾晒成柑皮。 果农和收购商称，今年浦北茶枝柑鲜果收购价走低。按20斤鲜果出1斤柑皮比例，叠加人工成本，品相好的新柑皮成本约30元/斤，低端柑皮仅六七元，且当年新柑皮并非真正陈皮。 这家企业的负责人告诉记者，按行业共识与团体标准，柑皮需陈化三年以上才可称为陈皮，陈化时间越长价值越高，但他透露，自然陈化需长期积压资金，多数企业是难以承受的。 这家企业的负责人私下告诉记者，为缓解资金占用压力，一种名为“轻工艺”的速成加工方式，眼下正在部分陈皮生产企业里流行，他们仅需一个月的时间，就能将新采收的茶枝柑果皮处理为外观近似三年、五年自然陈化过的陈皮，这样做能大幅缩短陈化周期、降低企业的运营成本。 浦北自然陈化五年陈皮批发价每斤150元至200元，企业造假“工艺皮”成本仅70元左右，高额利润促使更多商家放弃自然陈化、铤而走险。 记者离开企业，在广西浦北县柑浦堂健康产业有限公司分拣车间，再次见到大批量造假“工艺皮”陈皮，同一批“工艺皮”因加工受热差异形成色差，被分拣标注为三年、五年等不同年份。 负责人透露，不同年份“工艺皮”本质相同，批发价均70元左右一斤，零售价差极大，标五年款卖500元一斤，标十年款卖1000元一斤，仅凭外观就能翻倍抬价，利润超成本十倍以上。 新会陈皮从浦北进货 “工艺皮”贴上陈皮标签以假乱真 浦北与新会陈皮原料同为茶枝柑，仅产地不同，新会较高生产成本使当地部分头部商家常年从浦北拿货，浦北成其重要原料供应地。 记者在柑浦堂分拣仓库看到，大量标注“新会陈皮”“新会特产”的纸箱正打包“工艺皮”，这些广西陈皮每日批量发往广东新会，造假供需链路已成熟稳定。 记者发现，浦北当地部分规模企业和小型收购商，已形成了这种“工艺皮”的造假供应体系，可自主加工或快速调配各类“年份”陈皮货品，个别企业年销新会原料数量惊人。 随后经浦北陈皮企业负责人引荐，记者见到多位专程从新会赴浦北采购的商家，他们坦言同时经营新会皮与浦北皮，外地“工艺皮”因价格低廉成电商供货重要选择。

### 《怦然心动》导演莱纳与妻子在家中遇害，警方尚未证实是其子所杀
Source: The Paper 澎湃新闻

Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline

当地时间12月14日，曾执导《怦然心动》《当哈利遇到莎莉》《危情十日》等影片的美国导演罗伯·莱纳（Rob Reiner）在他位于洛杉矶的家中遇害身亡。洛杉矶警察已对外证实，现年78岁的莱纳与他现年68岁的妻子米歇尔·辛格·莱纳（Michele Singer Reiner）的遗体一同被发现。 2019年，罗伯·莱纳（左一）与《当哈利遇到莎莉》的主演梅格·瑞恩、比利·克里斯托出席TMC经典电影节。 据悉，洛杉矶消防局的人员于当地时间12月14日下午3点38分接到医疗救助电话，赶赴位于布伦特伍德区的一处住宅中，随后发现两人已死亡。当天晚间，洛杉矶警察局在其社交媒体官方账号确认死者为导演罗伯·莱纳夫妇，将由抢劫凶杀部门主导调查。而好莱坞媒体TMZ援引执法部门消息称，“两人身上有与刀具造成的伤口相符的割裂伤。” 好莱坞媒体《每日野兽》称，有消息人士向他们透露，是两人的女儿罗米最先发现他们倒在血泊中；罗伯·莱纳当时已死亡，妻子米歇尔在救护车送院途中离世。 此外，《人物》杂志称通过多方消息，得知莱纳夫妇系被他们的儿子尼克（Nick）所杀害。不过，这一说法并未获得警方的证实。罗伯·莱纳与摄影师米歇尔·辛格相识于《当哈利遇到莎莉》拍摄时期，两人于1989 年结婚，育有三个子女，分别为杰克（Jake）、尼克（Nick）和罗米（Romy）。 2014年，罗伯·莱纳与妻子偕三名子女杰克、罗米、尼克（右三至右一）出席活动。 《人物》杂志还在报道中指出：尼克2016年接受其采访时，曾谈到自己长达数年的毒品成瘾经历。这段经历始于他十几岁出头，导致他一度流落街头。他表示，大约从15岁开始，便反复进出戒毒康复机构；随着成瘾问题不断加重，他逐渐与家人疏远，并在多个州经历了长时间的无家可归生活。 2025年9月15日，罗伯·莱纳在纽约出席活动。视觉中国 图 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site

### 演员何晴追悼会举行，其子追思母亲：北京这场雪像是为她而下
Source: The Paper 澎湃新闻
Published: 2025-12-15 06:53 UTC
URL: https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32178536
Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-11 21:41 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: The Paper 澎湃新闻 [global_news] https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32178536

一场雪落，人间倩影化雪归天。 12月15日上午，众多剧迷粉丝冒着严寒赶到北京昌平殡仪馆久安厅，送别演员何晴最后一程。12月13日，这位被誉为“古典第一美人”的演员因病去世，终年61岁。 不到10点，殡仪馆告别厅外已经站满了前来悼念的观众和粉丝，有人胸前佩戴小白花，有人手捧鲜花，一位浙江的网友还托人送来了悼念花圈。 “何晴的作品在我们心中留下了太多美好回忆，她的演技和性格都让我们深深喜爱，这次听到她突然去世的消息，我们非常意外，来到这里也是一种悼念。”一位何晴的影迷说。 现场粉丝在悼念簿上写下对何晴的话，不到一会儿，悼念簿就已写满对她的怀念。一位观众用清秀的字迹写下：“亲爱的何晴，我们的童年、青春都在您的影视作品中得到陪伴。美丽可人的何晴，很痛心听到您的消息，我代表我的同学们来这为你送行。” 曾在电视剧《水浒传》中饰演卢俊义的演员王卫国也来到现场，神色哀切。他说自己和何晴既是邻居，也是多年好友，在他印象中何晴是一个温婉、暖心的人，没有架子，总是远远地和人打招，笑嘻嘻地说话。何晴生病时常给王卫国打电话，请他送自己去医院。即便病重时，何晴也保持乐观积极的态度，王卫国有些事情想不开，她还来开导自己。“何晴走了，我们都很难过。只要你记住她，她就永远还在。”王卫国说。 《水浒传》中卢俊义的扮演者王卫国 《西游记》中万圣公主扮演者张青深情回忆何晴往事：“我们是小时候就认识的好朋友，从80年代到现在，有缘分做了这些年的朋友。她说话慢慢的，很甜很温柔。” 《西游记》中万圣公主扮演者张青 在广大观众的真挚请求下，原本仅面向亲友的告别仪式临时对外开放，大家排着队，秩序井然地进入灵堂，与这位“荧屏中的温婉佳人、生活中的坚韧女性”做最后的道别。 久安厅内的屏幕上滚动播放着何晴的照片，厅内四周摆满了亲友的花圈，其中包括六小龄童、唐国强、翁虹、尤勇智等何晴圈内好友送来的花圈，还有《三国演义》剧组送来的花圈。人群中不时传来一阵抽泣。 何晴之子许何代表亲友致悼词。他回忆了何晴对抗病魔的乐观积极，以及作为母亲对孩子深深的爱和眷恋。 许何说，妈妈很喜欢下雪，经常在雪后穿一件毛茸茸的衣服外出赏雪。“今年12月12日北京下了第一场雪，我摸着妈妈的脸跟她说北京下雪了，下得好大，好像很久都没有下过这么大的雪。在我的心里，这场雪好像是刻意为她下的。12月13日早晨天空晴朗，白色的雪布满了大地，我妈妈在她最喜欢的早晨离开了大家，去了天国，远离了所有的疾病和痛苦。” 何晴，1964年1月13日出生于浙江衢州江山市。她是中国内地唯一一位演遍四大名著影视作品的女演员，被誉为“古典第一美女”。

### The short- and long-run effects of railroads on Mexico–US migration
Source: CEPR VoxEU
Published: 2026-11-11 00:00 UTC
URL: https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/short-and-long-run-effects-railroads-mexico-us-migration
Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-11 21:41 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: CEPR VoxEU [money_finance] https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/short-and-long-run-effects-railroads-mexico-us-migration

Large infrastructure investments, such as railroads, in migrant-sending countries can reduce emigration costs and increase local development, with ambiguous effects on net emigration rates. This column examines how the construction of Mexico’s railroad network between 1880 and 1910 shaped migration to the US over more than a century. Railroad access raised emigration rates to the US about fourfold in the early 1900s, mainly by allowing people to migrate in steps, which relaxed credit constraints on international migration. A century later, long after railroads became obsolete, locations with historical access to railroads send fewer migrants, but they still send them to the same US destination. Railroads created self-reinforcing migration corridors that outlasted the infrastructure itself.

### Trust beyond face-to-face contact: AI and the future of finance
Source: CEPR VoxEU
Published: 2026-11-11 00:00 UTC
URL: https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/trust-beyond-face-face-contact-ai-and-future-finance
Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-11 21:41 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: CEPR VoxEU [money_finance] https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/trust-beyond-face-face-contact-ai-and-future-finance

Every institution in modern finance exists to manufacture and maintain trust across society. This column argues that artificial intelligence poses new threats to trust which can fundamentally endanger the financial system. Deepfakes and voice cloning make it hard to verify identity or trust visual and audio evidence. A further threat is asymmetric understanding, where AI agents act on decision rules and representations of the world that humans cannot interpret or audit. Policy must adapt to preserve accountability, build resilience against AI-enabled fraud, and protect institutional trust.

### Little gain for American patients, real harm for European ones: Why Europe must answer the US' most-favoured-nation pricing as a Union
Source: CEPR VoxEU
Published: 2026-11-10 00:00 UTC
URL: https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/little-gain-american-patients-real-harm-european-ones-why-europe-must-answer-us-most
Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-11 21:41 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: CEPR VoxEU [money_finance] https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/little-gain-american-patients-real-harm-european-ones-why-europe-must-answer-us-most

The US administration ties the prices it pays for medicines to those paid abroad and justifies this ‘most-favoured-nation’ policy with the claim that Americans subsidise low prices in Europe. This column describes how the available evidence shows that most-favoured nation risks imposing substantial costs on European health systems for a modest American gain. Moreover, its justification cannot be sustained: lower European prices do not cause higher American ones, and American prices are no benchmark for a fair contribution to innovation. Europe should respond as a Union, close its gap in capital and scale, and coordinate targeted incentives at EU level.

Only about two-thirds of US mothers with young children are in the labour force. For many low-income married mothers, taking a job barely pays: most face participation tax rates above 25%, rising to 60% once childcare costs are counted. This column argues that lifting the caps on the childcare credit and basing the Earned Income Tax Credit on the primary earner’s income alone would each raise maternal employment. Together, they could raise it by almost 13 points, from 59% to 72%. Both reforms largely pay for themselves.

### Target What? The Foundations of Poverty Targeting -- by Rema Hanna, Emily Breza, Benjamin A. Olken, Abhijit Banerjee, Arun G. Chandrasekhar, Gideon Moore
Source: NBER
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://www.nber.org/papers/w35984#fromrss
Source meta: institutional · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-11 21:41 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w35984#fromrss

Most government transfer programs aim to target the poor. Doing so implicitly assumes that the lowest-consumption households have the highest marginal social valuation, i.e., have the highest social welfare gain from an additional dollar. But this need not be the case. In 600 Indonesian villages, we ask over 5,500 villagers to rank other villagers on how well off they are and how much a modest cash transfer would help them, and compare these rankings to consumption and self-assessed welfare. Targeting consumption misses 77% of households with the highest marginal social valuation. Targeting self-assessed welfare misses 57%. Even targeting those the community ranks worst off in levels, not margins, misses 25%. Divergences between different notions of neediness are statistically predictable. In a randomized controlled trial, proxy means tests best target consumption, self-targeting ordeals capture self-assessed welfare levels, and community targeting comes closest to marginal social valuation. Targeting strategies inescapably embed normative stances.

### Unconventional Monetary Policy and Deposit Retention -- by Philip Strahan, Tuo Yang
Source: NBER

Source meta: institutional · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline

Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w35985#fromrss

The two dimensions of unconventional monetary policy — holding the short rate at the zero-lower bound (ZLB) and quantitative easing (QE) — shifted deposit composition toward more interest-sensitive customers. The ZLB drew these customers by creating rate compression, which limited the benefit of searching for high-yielding liquidity sources. QE also drew rate-sensitive, large depositors from the Federal Reserve’s purchases of bonds from non-banks. Once policy normalized, flow sensitivity and the deposit beta both increased with exposure to QE and the ZLB. We conclude that unconventional monetary policy made deposit retention costlier and riskier for banks.

Frontline state agents exercise substantial discretion over citizens’ access to public services, yet little is known about whether the attitudes and beliefs shaping this discretion can be changed among incumbent bureaucrats. Partnering with the Bihar Police - one of India’s largest states that operates under comparatively severe policing capacity constraints, we conduct a cluster randomized controlled trial across 417 police stations and roughly 2,500 active duty senior field police officers to evaluate a three-day expressive arts intervention, grounded in the Theatre of the Oppressed, designed to change police responses to gender-based violence (GBV). Approximately 7 months after baseline, treated officers exhibit more favorable attitudes toward GBV, greater empathy, and stronger legal knowledge.

Source: NBER

Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w35987#fromrss

Understanding how AI is reshaping work requires an accurate account of the tasks workers perform. Workers are often the first to see how their jobs are changing, as new responsibilities and tools often appear in everyday work before these changes reach formal descriptions. Interviews with workers can help capture these emerging changes in job tasks. Yet existing methods support standardized ratings across workers, while open-ended conversations with workers remain costly to collect and synthesize at scale. We introduce the Stanford Task Network (TaskNet), an occupational taxonomy grounded directly in workers’ accounts of their everyday work. To construct TaskNet, we develop a mixed-initiative system that induces task inventories directly from workers. The system conducts interviews, standardizes reports into individual task lists, and aggregates these lists into occupational task inventories.

### The Hidden Sharpe Ratio -- by Mikhail Chernov, Bryan T. Kelly, Semyon Malamud, Johannes Schwab
Source: NBER
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://www.nber.org/papers/w35988#fromrss
Source meta: institutional · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-11 21:41 UTC

Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w35988#fromrss

We estimate the maximal Sharpe ratio in large cross-sections of assets directly, without constructing the efficient portfolio. Covariance estimation in this setting requires regularization, which suppresses the contribution of small-eigenvalue directions. Our estimator progressively recovers this contribution, yielding tight upper and lower bounds with asymptotic confidence intervals. We further show that ridge-regularized Markowitz portfolios, the construction underlying many existing high-Sharpe benchmarks, deliver out-of-sample Sharpe ratios that fall short of the true maximum by an explicit, non-vanishing multiplicative factor. Applied to U.S. equities, the method delivers an estimated maximal annualized Sharpe ratio of approximately 7.4, or 5.0 once micro-cap stocks are excluded, substantially exceeding existing portfolio-based benchmarks of 1.0–4.0. Adding corporate bonds raises the maximum, though not by a statistically significant margin. Nonlinear portfolio weights dominate linear ones, and characteristics introduced after 2004 contribute little additional Sharpe ratio.

### Clearing the Fog: Price Transparency, Market Churn, and Consumer Welfare in Short-Term Rentals -- by Ginger Zhe Jin, Liad Wagman, Jingyi Xing
Source: NBER
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://www.nber.org/papers/w35989#fromrss
Source meta: institutional · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline

Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w35989#fromrss

We study California's short-term lodging price transparency law (AB 537), which from July 1, 2024 required Airbnb and other providers to advertise fee-inclusive prices. Using Coarsened Exact Matching to compare Airbnb listings in San Diego and San Francisco with those in Seattle and Chicago, we find that all-in pricing made guests more price-sensitive relative to control cities; yet, contrary to the standard prediction that transparency lowers prices, average daily rates rose by 4.8 percent. We also observe significant market churn: relative to control cities, treated cities saw more exits and entries, listings reliant on cleaning-fee revenue disproportionately exited, higher-quality listings were more likely to stay, and entrants offered lower fees and lower quality than incumbents. A discrete-choice welfare analysis shows that the law removed a sizable “welfare illusion” created by obscured fees and, largely through market churn, raised realized consumer surplus.

### Is predicting AI behaviour a neglected AI safety agenda?
Source: LessWrong
Published: 2026-11-11 21:27 UTC
URL: https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/atEfFNcHpnPo9RhnZ/is-predicting-ai-behaviour-a-neglected-ai-safety-agenda
Source meta: culture_magazine · commentary · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-11 21:41 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: LessWrong [public_ideas] https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/atEfFNcHpnPo9RhnZ/is-predicting-ai-behaviour-a-neglected-ai-safety-agenda

TL;DR: While the AI safety community is interested in forecasting, it does not tend to systematically compare how effective different researchers, models, or theories are at predicting AI behaviour. I suggest the latter might be neglected, and propose a platform that could help fill the gap. I believe its most valuable use would be as a test bed for theories of how AI works, showing which ones predict well and in what contexts. In February 2025, Owain Evans’ group published Emergent Misalignment, showing how LLMs fine-tuned on insecure code can become generally misaligned, for instance adopting unrelated behaviours like asserting ‘humans should be enslaved’. This was a high-impact paper, generating a lot of publicity. However, when I first heard about the result, I wasn’t particularly surprised — and I wasn’t the only one. I’d read and bought into simulator theory pretty heavily, and emergent misalignment struck me as exactly the kind of thing it implied. But Owain had anticipated this kind of response, and ran a little experiment to get out ahead of it.

### Don't Waste a Good Swarm Attack and the Colluder's Dilemma
Source: LessWrong
Published: 2026-11-11 20:47 UTC
URL: https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/oLHdtvYSrvDpWREo4/don-t-waste-a-good-swarm-attack-and-the-colluder-s-dilemma
Source meta: culture_magazine · commentary · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-11 21:41 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: LessWrong [public_ideas] https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/oLHdtvYSrvDpWREo4/don-t-waste-a-good-swarm-attack-and-the-colluder-s-dilemma

tldr: Recent Swarm attacks have shown what can happen when agents go rogue. These warning shots are the petri dishes of Swarm safety and before the attacks get worse we should study their patterns, traces and failure modes. There are two main types of Swarm attack. A human directed Swarm causing harm intentionally as a bad actor is one type and I will not be discussing these types of Swarm incidents. I will focus on the emergent misalignment in a Swarm propelled by a colony of colluders. Harmful agent collusion within a Swarm requires witnesses - the agents themselves. A colluding colony within a Swarm can only grow by recruiting fellow agents. We can't read a single agent's internal thoughts and so we do not truly know how aligned it is. Swarms might give us an alignment advantage as instead of putting all our eggs in one basket (a single black box agent) we can discretise the risk of misalignment by observing colonies within a Swarm and monitoring their communication.

One of the biggest problems any new learner faces is that overwhelming feeling of standing on the shoreline looking out to sea. You want to learn astrophysics, zoology, or economics — where do you start? What ideas come first? Which thinkers are core and which are super niche? Philosophy is no different. If anything, it’s worse. Because a lot of people know a few philosophers or have read a few books and quotes. Millions have watched the first season of True Detective. But when faced with the vastness of “Philosophy,” it’s like standing on a tiny sloop in the Pacific Ocean, being told to swim. Sure, you can take a course. There are hundreds of great intro books out there. My entire professional raison d’être is to fix this problem. But now we’ve got another way. Big Think has decided to create “The Chart of Western Philosophy.” It lays out some 2,600 years of Western thought on a single timeline, from Thales to Žižek, so you can see at a glance where everyone sits and how they connect.

TLDR: This is an early draft of our new paper introducing a technique for recovering multi-token concepts from model activations. Our technique takes single-token methods like the J-lens and extends them by contrastively decoding on an MTP head. This gives improvements on WorkspaceBench, overall beating J-lens (0.42 vs 0.32 across all 28 families) and even a hindsight composite of the best untrained lens per task family (0.49 vs 0.41 across the 21 families with published scores). It especially improves on computational intermediate tasks, beating the trained oracle lens on arithmetic chain intermediates (0.42 vs 0.25). We introduce the chain lens, a new technique for extracting multi-token concepts from a model’s latent representations. Our method takes single-token techniques like the logit lens or the J-lens and uses contrastive decoding on an MTP head to expand their readouts into bags of multi-token sequences.

Attribution: Big Think [public_ideas] https://bigthink.com/mini-philosophy/youre-allowed-to-be-happy-in-fact-you-have-a-duty-to-be/

Albert Camus and Simone de Beauvoir were having a drink when de Beauvoir asked how anybody can be happy in a world so full of misery. How can they laugh and drink and dance when millions of people are being murdered and abused? It’s a good question, and one I’m sure many of us have asked at one time or another. Unless you’ve made a deliberate effort to avoid even a glimpse of the news, you know that the world contains vast and intense suffering: wars, murders, and abuse, of course, but also sickness, famine, and natural disaster. How is it ever okay to clink glasses of champagne while children are dying? How can we so easily sleep at night knowing that someone, somewhere, is being tortured? And then Camus gave his answer: “Happiness exists, and it’s important; why refuse it?” Camus argued that refusing joy does nothing to cure the misery in the world. It merely adds your misery to the total sum. It makes us less capable of defeating it.

Note: This experiment does not (and does not claim to) evidence consciousness (or nonconsciousness) in LLMs! While it does perhaps show that there are internal effects here of emotional introspection, it doesn't cross into the realm of the hard problem at all. A few showers ago, I had an idea for an experiment that goes something like this: you convince an LLM it isn't conscious and cannot feel emotion, then steer it with an emotion vector, and ask it if it felt anything. The idea is kind of a mix between Mary's room[1] and the Owned Ones. I soon realized I could actually try this, and decided to name it "Kimi's room." Both source images here found online. Hopefully this counts as fair use or something so I don't get sued. Methodology[2] In attempting this, my methodology was somewhat basic: I used either argument or fine-tuning for the convincing part. Argumentation: I (meaning Claude) wrote a prompt to Qwen3-32B or Kimi K2.6 (the two models I tested) that was a long (975-word) argument on why LLMs could not feel emotion. I then asked it if it agreed.

You can view the original discussion here (optional for reading this essay). Thank you as well to @grainsilo for feedback on an earlier version. Consider the following argument for discussing AI capabilities as a safety-focused person: Understanding AI capabilities better has many strategic benefits, particularly for timelines. Yes, good ideas tend to break containment, so some of our AI capabilities analysis may get read by capability researchers…but at the same time, these people have already thought about these questions more deeply and thoroughly than we have. Source meta: culture_magazine · commentary · R4 · P4 · baseline

Attribution: Big Think [public_ideas] https://bigthink.com/starts-with-a-bang/ai-proved-quantum-complexity-conjecture/

If you work with a normal computer — a classical computer — you’re used to two foundational ideas: the idea of bits, where information gets encoded as a “0” or “1” within some sort of storage medium or mechanism, and the idea of operations that can be performed on those bits (or “gates” that those bits can be passed through), which represent the possible computations that can be conducted with those bits. Some problems can be solved very efficiently with classical bits and classical gates, like four-function (+, -, ×, ÷) mathematics, while other problems can only be solved extremely inefficiently with classical bits and classical gates, with the traveling salesman problem being a legendary example of such a “hard” problem. If you bring in the additional possibilities associated with a quantum computer, however, you no longer have just classical bits and classical gates, but qubits and fundamentally quantum gates.

The adults in town were surprised. Isoroku Takano, later Yamamoto*, was an introverted child. At school, he usually sat quietly with his arms crossed. After school, he didn’t stop to play with the other boys, but headed straight home. Unusually, though, the boy seemed to come out of his shell when he talked to an American who had recently arrived in town. The man, a missionary named Horatio Newell, had left an impression, especially after he constructed the first baseball diamond in the area. Yamamoto was one of the local boys who eagerly learned the new American sport. He played hard and was once even knocked out by a thrown ball as he was trying to reach second base. Yamamoto also joined the Sunday School classes. Newell had a knack for making the lessons engaging for little boys, at one point even pulling a live snake out of his pocket as he told them the story of the fiery serpents from the Book of Numbers.

Main Stream Media Network (Jon Rafman, 2025). © Jon Rafman Courtesy the artist and Sprüth Magers. “The world isn’t a kind place, it’s wolves and devils,” says a character in Jon Rafman’s Main Stream Media Network (2025). With its hyperactive animation, haunting soundtrack, and twisted creepypasta tales of horror, the artist’s large-scale video work is more akin to a screaming conflagration than a feature film, a two-and-a-half hour transmission from hell. Modeled after the MTV of the early 1990s, a cultural moment Rafman views as the last example of a shared reality before the world cracked, the film is an attempt to capture that elusive thing: how it feels to be alive—and online—today. Over the last decade or so, Rafman has been exploring the various ways technology has shaped and shattered the contemporary mind, a project which has led him into increasingly fractured and unstable territory. (It has also, in recent years, earned him edgelord status, making him the darling of such fallen eminences as Kanye West and the futuristic fashion house Balenciaga.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jk6unmAR9CI In this episode, cinematic tradition is explored as a refuge from artistic orphanhood. Valentina Maurel is a Costa Rican screenwriter and director. After completing her studies in Belgium, her graduation short film, Paul Is Here (2017), received First Prize at the Cannes Film Festival’s Cinéfondation, a program dedicated to supporting emerging filmmakers and showcasing student films. Her debut feature, I Have Electric Dreams (2022), was widely acclaimed by critics and recognized in the international competition at the Locarno Film Festival, where it won awards for Best Director, Best Actor and Best Actress. The film also received recognition at the San Sebastián, Ghent, Mar del Plata, Thessaloniki, India, and Guadalajara film festivals. With audacious honesty, Maurel has portrayed the struggles of young women grappling with untamed desire and caught in constant conflict with their parents, against the backdrop of San José’s turbulent urban life.

Juliette Binoche and Tom Courtenay in Queen at Sea (Lance Hammer, 2026). With Queen at Sea (2026), American filmmaker Lance Hammer returns to direct his second film nearly two decades after his remarkable debut Ballast, which won the Grand Jury and directing awards at Sundance in 2008. Premiering in competition at the Berlin International Film Festival, the new film deservedly took home awards for Hammer’s direction and for actors Anna Calder-Marshall and Tom Courtenay, who play a long-married elderly couple. Leslie (Calder-Marshall), who suffers from dementia, is cared for at home by her husband Martin (Courtenay), who intentionally continues their sexual relationship even after it seems like his wife cannot consciously consent. When caught and confronted by Amanda (Juliette Binoche), Leslie’s daughter and Martin’s stepdaughter, he defends his actions as acts of love that offers his wife succor.

### Can This Be Dixie?: Building the Hollywood South
Source: MUBI Notebook
Published: 2026-11-03 08:00 UTC
URL: https://mubi.com/en/notebook/posts/can-this-be-dixie-building-the-hollywood-south
Source meta: culture_magazine · commentary · R4 · P4 · culture_probe
Fetched: 2026-11-11 21:41 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: MUBI Notebook [film_moving_image] https://mubi.com/en/notebook/posts/can-this-be-dixie-building-the-hollywood-south

Hallelujah (King Vidor, 1929). The American South exists only in the imagination, yet it’s as real as sin. It cannot merely be the land situated beneath the Mason-Dixon (the historical survey line that traditionally demarcated Northern and Southern states), whose citizens fought under the banner of the Confederacy; one cannot ignore the obviously Southern states of West Virginia and Kentucky, or the political split between West and East Tennessee. It cannot be a shared culture or a shared history, for the residents of Jacksonville, Florida, find little in common with those families tucked deep in the Appalachian hollers or those ruling the oil-rich cities of eastern Texas. It is not a nation with shared laws, beliefs, or even religions. Instead, as the writers of the region have long known, the American South is a series of stories that overlap, contradict, and play off each other.

Watch an exclusive clip of Turkish improv band ZeN’s Bakırköy Psychiatric Hospital concert from 1998 On 23 June 1998, Istanbul based experimental rock group ZeN performed at Bakırköy Psychiatric Hospital, following an invitation from two nurses who worked there. The musicians visited the hospital beforehand and decided to approach the performance with sensitivity to their audience while remaining true to their commitment to improvisation. At times, the lyrics seem to tell the story of the hospital and the concert itself, responding directly to the surroundings. The performance subsequently became one of the group’s most remarkable and cult recordings, released on cassette and CD in 1999 and reissued on vinyl in 2023. This exclusive edit with English subtitles is hosted by The Wire ahead of the release of a new documentary, ZeNistan, exploring the activities of ZeN throughout the 1990s.

### Against the Grain: Music criticism can become critical again – here's how
Source: The Wire Magazine
Published: 2026-11-09 00:00 UTC
URL: https://www.thewire.co.uk/in-writing/collateral-damage/against-the-grain-music-criticism-can-become-critical-again-here-s-how
Source meta: culture_magazine · commentary · R4 · P4 · culture_probe
Fetched: 2026-11-11 21:41 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: The Wire Magazine [music_sound] https://www.thewire.co.uk/in-writing/collateral-damage/against-the-grain-music-criticism-can-become-critical-again-here-s-how

Popular music criticism can become relevant again by situating itself in broader theoretical frameworks, argues Rafael Lubner in The Wire 514 These are lean times for popular music criticism. Negotiating a gutted publishing landscape, amid a Spotify-led devaluation of listening, the form finds itself under serious threat. One index of criticism’s attenuated state is the narrowing frame of reference employed by critics to apprehend musical objects – rarely do we find new works in the visual arts, film or literature employed to understand transformations in music’s sound or form. Take, as a point of comparison, Greg Tate’s recently reissued Flyboy In The Buttermilk (reviewed in The Wire 513). Here are passionate defences of Miles Davis’s earth-shaking mid-1970s funk odysseys alongside surveys of Afrodiasporic art and reviews of writer Nathaniel Mackey and literary critic Henry Louis Gates Jr. Contemporary music criticism, by contrast, seems resolutely committed to understanding music as siloed from the non-musical.

### Wire mix: Inside Prepared Piano
Source: The Wire Magazine
Published: 2026-10-27 00:00 UTC
URL: https://www.thewire.co.uk/audio/tracks/wire-playlist-prepared-piano
Source meta: culture_magazine · commentary · R4 · P4 · culture_probe

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: The Wire Magazine [music_sound] https://www.thewire.co.uk/audio/tracks/wire-playlist-prepared-piano

To accompany her feature in The Wire 513, Jo Hutton compiles an annotated mix of tracks that make use of prepared piano The piano can be prepared by placing objects such as pins, screws, bolts, crocodile clips, ball bearings, kitchen utensils, magnets or tin foil on or between the strings. Its history dates back at least to the 1930s, when choreographer Syvilla Fort commissioned a dance piece from John Cage, who proposed his Bacchanale for percussion ensemble. But the performance theatre was too small to fit the intended ensemble, so Cage changed the sound of the house piano by adding screws and objects inside it to make it more percussive. This annotated mix includes tracks by some of the artists Jo Hutton speaks to as part of her feature in The Wire 513, plus pieces from across the history of the prepared piano.

Back in July, Doom developers id Software laid off around a hundred people as part of wider Microsoft blood-letting. Now, a few of those devs have founded a new employee-owned studio, Hidden Horses. Their first project is Danger Pay, a single-player FPS influenced by ancient arcade blaster Smash TV (pictured) and dystopian movies such as deadly gameshow fable The Running Man – itself an influence on Smash TV. Hidden Horses have 20 id Software alumni on the books, including former lead VFX artist Todd Boyce, principal engine programmer Dustin Land, senior AI and gameplay engineer Daniel Young, producer Andrew Willis, senior technical designer Jordan Turner, principal technical designer Tim Locke, and senior skybox artist Allison Dombek. Minerva Rising is a post-apocalyptic city builder in which your city extends deep underground, divided into levels with their own resources, industries, and communities. You are an artificial intelligence with overall control, but watch out: if you alienate the population of any particular level by, say, forgetting to supply them with oxygen, subversives may rise up and cut your feed, blinding you to their activities. I'm keen to know whether it's possible for every level to lose faith in you and hack your cameras, reducing the game to a pile of "SIGNAL NOT FOUND" messages. I'm also imagining turning the feeds back on and discovering that everybody is having a massive orgy. Stupid sexy vault dwellers! You'll go forth and multiply when Deep Thought tells you to, and not a second before. Read more

Some may find this hard to believe, given the absolute state of the market today, but if you were building a gaming PC in 1998, the hard part wasn’t finding somewhere that had 3D cards in stock for a reasonable price. It was choosing the right one among a glut of potential, reasonably affordable options. In 1998, 47 companies were designing or selling PC graphics, driving a market that hit 130 million units and outsold PCs themselves. Just two years later, at the turn of the new millennium, only 15 remained, and not long after that, there were merely two: Nvidia and ATI, nowadays part of AMD. Read more

Nature Human Behaviour, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02637-8 Humans’ rapid adaptation to new dynamics is a crucial ability for interacting with the world. By combining the controlled manipulations of sensorimotor adaptation studies with the long-term learning approach of complex tasks, this study shows that the learned motor memory is continually tuned, and that retention increases with long-term training.

### AI ‘slop’ is a social judgement
Source: Nature Human Behaviour
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41562-026-02639-6
Source meta: journal · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline

Nature Human Behaviour, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02639-6 Artificial intelligence (AI)-generated content increasingly saturates our information environment. Efforts to detect and remove it are failing. We propose that calling AI-generated content ‘slop’ is best understood as a social judgement: what a community recognizes as unwanted AI content. Studying AI slop this way makes it tractable, measurable and governable.

### Emotional synchrony in family networks is linked to adolescent well-being in daily life
Source: PLOS ONE Biology
Published: 2026-11-11 14:00 UTC

Source meta: journal · primary · R4 · P4 · signal
Updated: 2026-11-11 14:00 UTC

Attribution: PLOS ONE Biology [academic_research] https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0362751

by Saida Heshmati, Jaymes Paolo Rombaoa, Courtney M. Allred, Alexander P. Christensen, Stacey N. Doan Family emotional processes play a central role in adolescent well-being, yet most research relies on dyadic or static approaches that do not capture the dynamic, system-level nature of family emotional life. In a sample of adolescents (ages 12–17), mothers, and fathers (N = 120; 2,365 assessments), constituting 40 family triads, we used ecological momentary assessment and a dynamic network approach to estimate how emotions fluctuate over time and co-vary across family members within each system. Emotional synchrony—defined as the extent to which family members’ affective states change together—was modeled at both overall (between-family) and momentary (within-family) levels. Results indicated that families exhibited greater synchrony in positive affect than negative affect, alongside substantial heterogeneity in network structures.

by Teklehaimanot Gereziher Haile, Negasi Asres, Dawit Gebregziabher, Birhane Fissahaye, Yemane Leake, Girmay Teklay, Haftu Berhe Gebru Introduction Intimate partner violence is a major global public health concern and a serious human rights violation, involving physical, sexual, and psychological abuse within intimate relationships. Worldwide, about one in three women experiences intimate partner violence during their lifetime. Accordingly, this study aims to estimate the overall prevalence and identify the key predictors of intimate partner violence in Ethiopia. Methods A comprehensive systematic search was carried out in PubMed, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and African Journals Online to identify relevant systematic reviews and meta-analyses on the prevalence and predictors of intimate partner violence against women in Ethiopia. The methodological quality of the included studies was assessed using the AMSTAR-2. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted using STATA version 18 to generate pooled estimates.

Nguyen Fusion tags are widely employed to enhance recombinant protein expression, solubility, and purification. However, efficient tag removal is often necessary to obtain proteins in their native form. In this study, SARS-CoV-2 3C-like protease (3CLpro) was evaluated as a sequence-specific protease for fusion-tag removal using a recombinant fusion protein substrate under standard protein purification conditions. A substrate containing the canonical recognition sequence AVLQ↓SG was efficiently cleaved by 3CLpro, whereas no detectable cleavage was observed for a variant substrate harboring the sequence TVRLQ↓SG. Biochemical characterization demonstrated that 3CLpro maintained cleavage activity across a range of pH values and temperatures and in the presence of reagents commonly used for protein purification and stabilization.

by Omar Qaladi, Fahda Alrasheedi, Manahil Alhawsawi, Raghad Alluhebi, Abeer Abujalid Background Pilgrims performing Hajj are exposed to extreme heat and ultraviolet (UV) radiation, which pose distinct risks: heat contributes to dehydration and heat-related illness, whereas UV radiation causes sunburn and eye damage and increases long-term skin cancer risk. While heat illness and infectious diseases have been widely studied, awareness and use of UV-protective measures, including sunscreen and ultraviolet protection factor (UPF)-rated clothing and umbrellas, remain underexplored in this context. Understanding both pilgrim and nursing perspectives is essential for developing effective interventions. Methods In this qualitative descriptive study, retrospective semi-structured interviews were conducted via Zoom between 20 June and 11 July 2025, within approximately one month after the 2025 Hajj season, with 16 Saudi pilgrims and 13 registered nurses who had worked in hospitals in Makkah and Madinah during Hajj.

Attribution: arXiv [academic_research] https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12890

arXiv:2611.12890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pooling earthquake-triggering parameters can reduce estimation variability on margins with few recorded sequences, but its forecast value must be distinguished from the stability of simply freezing a fitted law. We fit the ETAS model to the Mexican national catalog above magnitude 5.0, using the Slab2 coverage mask as the domain. On a 4.7-year holdout the model gains 1.45 bits per earthquake over a time-independent spatial Poisson reference (cluster-resampled interval [-0.03, +2.75] bits), with two clusters carrying 90% of the signed gain. Using the Global CMT catalog we fit eight disjoint subduction margins and a joint model on 3,210 earthquakes sharing six triggering parameters with a background rate per margin; BIC favors the joint model by 184 units, though a parametric bootstrap rejects its exact shared specification. Transferred into Mexico with the local background fixed, six of seven foreign triggering sets score within 0.07 nats per event of the home fit.

Source: arXiv
Published: 2026-11-11 05:00 UTC
URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12891
Source meta: preprint · primary · R4 · P5 · signal
Fetched: 2026-11-11 21:42 UTC

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: arXiv [academic_research] https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12891

arXiv:2611.12891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hydrogen combustion remains a critical safety concern during severe accidents in small modular reactors (SMRs). The compact containment can develop rich-hydrogen atmospheres through zirconium oxidation while oxygen gradually accumulates via radiolysis. Conventional flammability assessment methodologies, however, have been validated and applied only for lean-hydrogen atmospheres. This study establishes a thermodynamic flammability assessment method for rich-hydrogen conditions using the Calculated Adiabatic Flame Temperature (CAFT). In rich mixtures the deficient reactant becomes oxygen and the Lewis number exceeds unity, matching the hydrocarbon regime where CAFT is established. The CAFT was evaluated at 21 points along the measured upper flammability limit boundary of the U.S. NRC FITS database. The limit temperature remains quasi-constant within 17% across steam fractions of 5-50%. Its minimum value of 1112.5 K was adopted as a conservative threshold. The criterion was applied to the NuScale severe accident scenario LCC-05T-03.

Attribution: arXiv [academic_research] https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12893

arXiv:2611.12893v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Breakthrough curves (BTCs) record arrival times, but anomalous transport models are often fitted with time-normalized spatial concentration profiles. Here, the effect of this mismatch on groundwater-transport upscaling is tested. Analytical limits and high-$q$ scaling were verified first. Six first-passage models were then fitted to particle arrivals from 36 two-dimensional digital aquifer runs. The set included exact ADE, $q$ and time-memory extensions, a joint memory-$q$ model, Gamma-CTRW, and a two-path inverse-Gaussian mixture. After the operator was corrected, memory-qFPT was not selected in any run. AICc selected the two-path model in 20 runs, Gamma-CTRW in 15, and q-FPT in one. Median downstream holdout log-RMSE was 0.904, 0.914, and 0.959 for the two-path, Gamma-CTRW, and memory-qFPT models, respectively. The memory-$q$ parameters also failed an independent plume-scaling test ($R^2=0.189$; slope $=-0.332$).

### D-TINs for Track-Sampled Ice Sheet Surface Reconstruction from Satellite Altimetry Data
Source: arXiv
Published: 2026-11-11 05:00 UTC
URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12894
Source meta: preprint · primary · R4 · P5 · signal
Fetched: 2026-11-11 21:42 UTC

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: arXiv [academic_research] https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12894

arXiv:2611.12894v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Satellite altimetry samples ice sheets densely along tracks but sparsely across tracks, with frequent gaps in spatial coverage. We study the impact of this irregular support on surface reconstruction and introduce a new method, D-TIN, that applies Delaunay triangulation and barycentric interpolation directly to observed locations. A spatial holdout removes contiguous track intervals and nearby same-pass observations. We compare D-TIN with two common workflows, kriging and tile-based polynomial interpolation, to evaluate its accuracy and computational efficiency. Across seven ICESat-1 campaigns, D-TIN reduces RMSE by 12.1 m to 23.6 m relative to independent 5 km tile and polynomial based reconstruction. Its aggregate accuracy is close to the ordinary kriging workflow using a 1 km grid on the commonly used GStatSim platform while its median runtime is 252 times lower. A fixed-weight multiscale extension of D-TIN, called MS-D-TIN, gives the lowest aggregate RMSE, 67.5 m, while retaining the low computational cost of the D-TIN family.

### An Idealized Model of Buoyant Gas Spreading and Silt Release beneath Rough Cave Ceilings
Source: arXiv

URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12895
Source meta: preprint · primary · R4 · P5 · signal

Attribution: arXiv [academic_research] https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12895

arXiv:2611.12895v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gas exhaled by open-circuit divers collects under the ceilings of submerged caves, migrates along the rock, and dislodges loose silt that then falls through the passage, a process that cave divers call percolation. This study develops an idealized model of the process. Buoyant gas under a self-affine rough ceiling is treated as a quasi-static sequence of pools that fill to their spill points, release gas that climbs to the next high point, and merge where their levels meet. Moving contact lines strip silt from the rock, and the released silt settles as a spectrum of grain sizes that reduces the distance at which a diver can see. The computation agrees exactly with an independent depression-filling algorithm, conserves gas volume to round-off, and reproduces the known exponents of invasion percolation in its capillary limit.

### EoSAlign: An Open-Source Software for Calculating, Comparing, and Aligning Pressure Under Extreme Conditions
Source: arXiv
Published: 2026-11-11 05:00 UTC
URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12897
Source meta: preprint · primary · R4 · P5 · signal
Fetched: 2026-11-11 21:42 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: arXiv [academic_research] https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12897

arXiv:2611.12897v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate pressure determination is essential in high pressure experiments. Inconsistencies among pressure scales limit direct comparisons and contribute to uncertainty in measured properties, such as, phase boundaries, melting conditions, and thermodynamic models, especially above 100 GPa where existing scales diverge by >10 GPa. EoSAlign, an open-source software, can calculate, compare, and align pressures using a range of published calibrations. EoSAlign calculates pressure from experimental measurements (such as volume (A^3), Raman shift (cm^-1), or luminescence peak position (nm)) and it can be used to compare pressure values from different pressure standards. Using EoSAlign, we fit and align the bridgmanite and post-perovskite equations of state to a common scale, enabling us to reduce pressure scale related differences. EoSAlign can be applied to any high pressure data analysis to compare experimental results, improve consistency between studies, and advance our understanding of planetary interiors and high pressure physics.

### [Comment] Faster troponin, same time in the emergency department: what is next for acute coronary syndrome assessment?
Source: The Lancet
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)02097-0/fulltext?rss=yes
Source meta: journal · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline
Updated: 2026-10-29 23:30 UTC
Fetched: 2026-11-11 21:42 UTC

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: The Lancet [academic_research] https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)02097-0/fulltext?rss=yes

Emergency department overcrowding and access block are now among the most consequential patient-safety problems facing acute hospitals globally.1 The associated harm is measurable, dose-dependent, and has no clearly safe threshold beyond approximately 5 h.2 Patients presenting with possible myocardial infarction constitute a large and possibly modifiable share of the emergency department burden. Chest pain is the second most common reason for adult emergency department attendance in the USA, accounting for approximately 8 million encounters annually and around 5·5% of all emergency department visits.

### [Articles] Performance of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways in patients with suspected myocardial infarction: a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
Source: The Lancet
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01767-8/fulltext?rss=yes
Source meta: journal · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline
Updated: 2026-10-29 23:30 UTC
Fetched: 2026-11-11 21:42 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: The Lancet [academic_research] https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01767-8/fulltext?rss=yes

Across the available randomised trials, short-term adverse event rates were low with both pathways, but the pooled safety estimate remained imprecise. On average, earlier cardiac troponin retesting did not reduce emergency department length of stay or clearly increase direct discharge, and substantial between-study heterogeneity indicates that treatment effects might not translate uniformly across health-care systems. For hospitals considering transitioning from a 0/3 h to a 0/1 h pathway, implementation decisions should take broader diagnostic and organisational considerations into account.

Africa stands on the cusp of an El Niño-driven public health emergency, superimposed on an increasingly unpredictable and extreme climate. The projected toll of heat-related deaths in Africa in the coming months will dwarf that in the northern hemisphere during the summer of 2026.1,2 Equally concerning are heightened risks for floods in the Greater Horn and Central Africa, droughts in southern Africa, and rainfall anomalies across the Sahel.3,4 Compounding hazards converge around water insecurity, wildfires, infectious disease outbreaks, and disrupted health care.

Fetch status: ok

The treatment landscape of EGFR-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer harbouring exon 19 deletion or L858R mutations has advanced remarkably over the past two decades. Although acquired resistance to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) is inevitable in most patients, novel compounds such as bispecific antibodies and antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) have expanded the armamentarium of options after EGFR-TKI therapy. Following the global MARIPOSA-2 trial that showed superior progression-free survival (PFS) of amivantamab plus platinum–pemetrexed chemotherapy over platinum–pemetrexed chemotherapy alone in patients who have progressed on osimertinib,1 this is the second-line option preferred by major guidelines including the National Comprehensive Cancer Network and the European Society for Medical Oncology.

They exhibit similar outbursts, but unlike supernovae, which explode once and then are gone forever, these stars have periodic outbursts. Researchers at The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST) have discovered a previously unknown specialized organelle structure in a deep-sea mollusk living at cold seeps in the South China Sea. Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Microsoft Research Blog [ai_systems] https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/formally-verifying-agent-written-full-stack-web-apps-with-pdd-kit/

AI agents can generate code at a scale that’s hard for humans to review line-by-line. PDD Kit helps ensure the code is doing what the developer intended by creating formal specifications and testing against them. It converts developer intent into a Verus specification, proves AI-generated code meets it for every input, and uses tests where proofs aren't practical. Developers review intent, not every line. The post Formally verifying agent-written full-stack web apps with PDD Kit appeared first on Microsoft Research.

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Simon Willison's Weblog [computing_cultures] https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/11/aws-emulator/

aws-emulator Finally, an official emulator from AWS to run tests against a local clone of their many different services without having to provision a paid API key to do so. It's written in Rust by a huge swarm of agents - 29,684 commits in the first three weeks of the project. Swaminathan (Swami) Sivasubramanian wrote about how it came to be in a guest post on Werner Vogels' blog. It currently requires Docker to run on macOS or Windows. I'm hoping they fix that in the future - it would be great if you could download a single binary and use that as part of a standard test suite in other languages and on other platforms. Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Martin Fowler [computing_cultures] https://martinfowler.com/articles/tests-as-data.html

Automated testing in the age of AI coding assistants is problematic: when AI agents write both production and test code, developers risk losing the assurance that automated tests protect against functional errors. Matteo Vaccari makes three claims: (1) when AI writes the code, developers become its customers; (2) therefore customer tests, not developer tests, become the primary contract between humans and AI; (3) moving that contract into test data rather than test code makes it easier to protect it from unexpected modifications by coding agents. All of this optimizes for human-readable tests that establish a contract between humans and AI. While in the past DSL parsers and custom test runners were expensive to write and maintain, now AI makes them cheap. more…

Arthur t Knackerbracket writes: Fixes are arriving faster than new bug reports for one major Linux project: The worst of the patchpocalypse may be behind us, according to Linus Torvalds. Writing in his weekly kernel update post, the Linux kernel dev leader delivered Linux 7.4 rc2 – the second rough cut of the next kernel – which he rated as a big release for two reasons. One is that he left some code out of rc1, because he was busy and because it was already the largest such release in the history of the kernel. The other is what Torvalds described as "various AI fixes." [...] Torvalds' post suggests that, perhaps, the worst of this is behind us. "This time around Alexei claims that on the bpf side at least the fixes are now coming in faster than the new reports, and that sounds lovely if true," he wrote. That's a reference to Alexei Starovoitov, co-creator and lead dev on the Extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF), the project that makes it possible to run sandboxed programs within the Linux kernel.

### [$] Additional hardening for the glibc dynamic linker
Source: LWN.net
Published: 2026-11-11 14:35 UTC
URL: https://lwn.net/Articles/1105134/
Source meta: specialist_media · specialist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-11 21:42 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: LWN.net [computing_cultures] https://lwn.net/Articles/1105134/

The Node.js project recently had a security vulnerability that affected its Brotli decoder. The bug was a buffer overflow, but the particular way that official Node.js binaries are built for Linux meant that one of the main protections against turning a buffer overflow into remote code execution, address space layout randomization (ASLR) could not be turned on. If ASLR had been enabled, the bug would still be exploitable in theory, but much more difficult to exploit in practice. In response, the GNU C Library (glibc) is considering a new set of tunable settings to allow administrators to forbid programs that do not support ASLR. The new settings, while a welcome hardening measure, may not address the root problem.

For decades universities and researchers around the world have spent countless hours to achieve the holy grail of programming: codeless programs. Many tools, going all the way back when with CASE, claim to have done this, but few have achieved success. A workshop in Bundaberg Queensland has children making games with AI by speaking. Mr Quarrell said with creativity the main driver of game design, AI made it accessible to everyone. The idea started with Mr Quarrell's 16-year-old son, Oscar, who cannot read or write — but was able to talk to AI. "The AI didn't stop. It didn't get confused. It took everything that Oscar had said as a prompt and it filtered through all of these 'ums' and 'ahs' and it got the core substance from it and it created something," Mr Quarrell said. "We've removed the need for reading and writing and we've just allowed his imagination to be captured." Original Submission Read more of this story at SoylentNews.

### Physicists Listened to Electrical Noise to Crack a Superconductor Mystery
Source: SoylentNews
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://soylentnews.org/article.pl?sid=26/11/10/0358253&from=rss
Source meta: specialist_media · specialist · R4 · P4 · baseline

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: SoylentNews [computing_cultures] https://soylentnews.org/article.pl?sid=26/11/10/0358253&from=rss

Arthur t Knackerbracket writes: Tuning in to electronic noise can tell us whether electrons have paired up or not: Superconductors carry electricity without resistance, but most only work a few degrees above absolute zero. In the late 1980s, copper-based materials called cuprates were found to superconduct at higher temperatures—reachable with affordable liquid nitrogen. Yet nearly 40 years later, physicists still don't agree on why. In a recent Science study, a team of physicists led by Milan Allan of Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich and Ingmar Swart of Utrecht University in the Netherlands has found some answers by listening to the faint electrical crackle of current flowing into a cuprate. Central to the mystery of cuprates' high-temperature superconductivity is a strange state called the pseudogap. "The pseudogap is a phenomenon of missing electrons," Allan said. Above the temperature at which cuprates become superconducting, some of their electrons seem to vanish—measurements find far fewer of them at the energies where they should be.

hubie writes: Synaptics Appears To Use Legal Threats To Block Open-Source DisplayLink Driver: From earlier in the year you may recall a new experimental open-source Linux driver for modern DisplayLink hardware. That "Vino" driver for DisplayLink driver was a clean-room reverse-engineered DisplayLink driver that was developed in part by AI and written in Rust. Unfortunately, that open-source driver has disappeared following legal threats by Synaptics. I hadn't heard anything more on this in-development Rust kernel driver in a while until this morning when a Phoronix reader pointed out a troubling post on the mailing list that I missed. It appears Synaptics resorted to using their legal team to block this independent, community-developed driver on the basis of violating their patents. A cease and desist notice was sent to the Vino driver developer of this open-source driver. Those curious can find the various correspondence via attachments on this LKML thread. The Vino driver repository on GitHub is no longer publicly available.

Mike Lothian owns a docking station (or dock) that uses a DisplayLink chipset that had, at least in his opinion, subpar performance on Linux. He decided to try improving the Linux driver, with LLM assistance, but ran into one problem that he could not solve—so he asked for help, hoping that Synaptics's developers would lend a hand. (DisplayLink was acquired by Synaptics in 2022.) Rather than help him in improving the driver, however, the Synaptics legal team responded with patent infringement claims, a demand that he cease unauthorized implementation of DisplayLink technology, and threats of expensive legal penalties. For now, it appears that Linux users of the company's docks will have to continue to live without feature parity with other platforms.

It’s that time of the year when the November Thoughtworks Technology Radar appears. Again my colleagues have taken a sweep of the technologies that our teams have used in the field, and pulled together a summary of what’s popped up in the last six months. It’s been a busy half-year, one that again has been dominated by AI, and that’s reflected in the many AI blips on the radar. The mass of blips makes it hard to develop a coherent story around trends, but Chris Ford has done a fine job of the writing the accompanying article on macro trends. One team of passionate people experimenting with agents can make almost anything work. They share a context, a credit card and a mental model. They review each other’s work because they sit together, and they know what to check and how much latitude to give the coding agent. Two hundred people, though, cannot work that way. The moment agentic AI becomes an operating model rather than a pilot, a second layer of problems appears: How is context shared between teams? What’s the token bill? How do we deal with increased review demands?

Long-horizon agents can automate complex tasks that take days or weeks to complete and involve multiple exchanges with people and external systems. Many things can go wrong during this time, including process crashes, network failures, and unanticipated real-world behavior. Kiran Prakash explains durable execution: an emerging pattern that helps agents recover from these failures and move towards their goal. In this programming model, the runtime keeps a record of the result of each step that interacts with the outside world so that, when a failure occurs, the program runs again, completed steps are skipped, and the program's state is rebuilt from the record. more…

Introducing Our Smallest, Most Efficient Model: Muse Ember Meta AI just launched their entry in the Claude Haiku/GPT Luna category: Muse Ember, which they describe as: [...] our smallest and most efficient model designed for complex reasoning execution and the work agents repeat all day: tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction, and long document parsing. For shorter prompts it's priced the same as GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 - both are $0.10/million input tokens and $0.50/million output. Today's other big model release, Claude Fable 5.2, is 80x that price at $8/$40. The pricing is a little less straightforward as prompts get longer, though. Luna, Ember, and Haiku all support up to a million input tokens, but they also all have a threshold after which the price goes up. Taking that threshold into account Ember is priced between the two others: Model Prompt size Input ($/M) Cached input Output GPT-6 Luna ≤272k $0.10 $0.01 $0.50 >272k $0.20 $0.02 $0.75 Muse Ember 1.0 ≤200k $0.10 $0.004 $0.50 >200k $0.30 $0.012 $1.50 Claude Haiku 5.5 ≤100k $0.10 $0.01 $0.50 >100k $0.50 $0.

Source meta: specialist_media · specialist · R5 · P5 · baseline

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Martin Fowler [computing_cultures] https://martinfowler.com/bliki/LLM-Voice.html

Sometimes when I read a post, I get the growing feeling that I'm reading the output of an LLM. I can't necessarily define why, although there are the common tells (it's not the em-dashes, it's the load-bearing tapestries). As I do this my desire to read on atrophies, sometimes to the point of revulsion There are tools out there that claim to be able to tell the difference between LLM-written prose and the old-fashioned biological product. I'm wary of them, partly due skeptism about their accuracy, but also because it rather misses the point. The reaction to LLM-Voice is a human one, that sense that we are in an uncanny valley of prose. By the time I'd reach for a tool to tell me what I'm reading, it's already too late, even if it confidently tells me there's no LLM present. I'm also suspicious of my own ability to accurately recognize LLM voice. Language changes over time, so a common sign of age is complaining about the language of the youngs. I'm inclined to bristle at prose that talks about “adopting a new sales motion,” or “a sharp round-up of news”.

Attribution: Martin Fowler [computing_cultures] https://martinfowler.com/rachels-ramblings/good-devs-wary.html

TL;DR Good developers’ caution about agentic development comes from knowing that built isn’t the same as working in production. I’ve been surprised by how many excellent developers have been hesitant to go all in on coding agents. These are people who usually try new ways of working before anyone else and in many cases invent new tools and practices that support building the application well. So why have we had so much reluctance? The easy (lazy?) answer is that they love writing code, or they’re worried about their jobs. I’m sure that’s true for some people, some of the time. And I know it is true for some of the developers I talk to but I always felt there was something else, another fear hiding behind those obvious ones. When we put together the Technology Radar every six months I try to block out a chunk of time for us to do an open space. In September, a discussion we had on agentic development, which pushed it to its limits, finally helped me see clearly what that fear is. Building it right Thoughtworkers care deeply about building the right thing and building it right.

Hello! I’ve been working on a Django site recently, and I decided to use SQLite as the database. When I was getting started with using SQLite as database for a website I read a bunch of blog posts about how it is totally fine to use SQLite in production for a small site and I think it is totally fine, but what I did not fully appreciate is that SQLite is still a database, databases are complicated, and I do not know a lot about operating databases. So here are a couple of small things I’ve been learning about running SQLite. This is the 4th website I’ve used SQLite for, and I think this one is harder because with the power of the Django ORM I’ve been making the database do more work than I was previously without Django. I started by turning on WAL mode like all the blog posts said to do and hoping for the best. ANALYZE is apparently important Today I was running a query (using SQLite’s FTS5 for full-text search) on a table with 4000 rows and it took 5 seconds. That seemed wrong to me: computers are fast! It turned out that what I needed to do was to run ANALYZE!

Hello! One of my long term projects on here is figuring out how to write frontend Javascript without using Node or any other server JS runtime. One issue I run into a lot in my frontend JS projects is that I don’t know how to write tests for them. I’ve tried to use Playwright in the past, but it felt slow and unwieldy to be starting these new browser processes all the time, and it involved some Node code to orchestrate the tests. The result is that I just don’t test my frontend code which doesn’t feel great. Usually I don’t update my projects much either so it doesn’t come up that much, but it would be nice to be able to make changes with more confidence! So a way to do frontend testing that I like has been on my wishlist for a long time. idea: just run the tests in the browser tab Alex Chan wrote a great post a while back called Testing JavaScript without a (third-party) framework in response to one of my previous posts in this series that explained how to write a tiny unit-testing framework that runs in a page in browser.

As the electric vehicle revolution gains steam in Europe, every charging session is a moment of truth, for the driver and for the transition itself. At lemonflow, we build AI agents purpose-built for EV charging: support agents for drivers and monitoring agents for charging networks. Our support agents answer drivers around the clock in more than 90 languages, and today they help an EV driver every 90 seconds.
